gaps.sentence: When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my security pass.
gaps.hint: the forgetting happened before realising it
gaps.explanation: The forgetting happened before the past moment of realising, so the past perfect is needed: had forgotten.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our cousins in Melbourne next month — the flights are booked.
gaps.hint: a booked arrangement for next month
gaps.explanation: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: are visiting.

gaps.sentence: We ___ each other since primary school, so nothing surprises me about him.
gaps.hint: since primary school continuing to now
gaps.explanation: A state continuing since a past point takes the present perfect: have known.

gaps.sentence: By the end of the month, they ___ the new bridge.
gaps.hint: by the end of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a specific future point takes the future perfect: will have finished.

gaps.sentence: She is exhausted because she ___ since dawn.
gaps.hint: since dawn explains her present exhaustion
gaps.explanation: An action running from the past to now and explaining a present state takes the present perfect continuous: has been travelling.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ for over two hours.
gaps.hint: for over two hours up to now
gaps.explanation: A duration continuing up to the present moment takes the present perfect continuous: have been chatting.

gaps.sentence: This jacket ___ to my brother, so please do not take it by mistake.
gaps.hint: belong is always a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Belong' is a state verb and has no continuous form, so the present simple is correct: belongs.
